title: Potential form (〜られる / 〜える) "can do"
meaning: Expresses ability ("can", "be able to") or possibility.
simpleExplanation: The potential form turns a verb into "can do". 読む (read) becomes 読める (can read), 食べる (eat) becomes 食べられる (can eat). Think of it as building "can" into the verb itself instead of adding a separate word. Once you have made the potential form, it behaves like an ordinary Group 2 verb, so 読める → 読めます / 読めない / 読めた.
whenUsed: Used everywhere, at every politeness level, for ability (漢字が読める = I can read kanji), for possibility (ここで買える = you can buy it here) and for permission-like situations on signs (ここでは泳げません = you cannot swim here). It is the everyday alternative to 〜ことができる, which sounds more formal.
formation: Group 1: change the last う-row sound to the え-row and add る: 書く→書ける, 読む→読める, 話す→話せる, 待つ→待てる
Group 2: drop る and add られる: 食べる→食べられる, 見る→見られる
Group 3: する→できる, 来る→来られる
The result is a Group 2 verb: 読めます / 読めない / 読めた / 読めて
The object normally takes が (漢字が読める), though を is also heard

diagram.root: 書く / 食べる / する / 来る

examples.reading: わたしは かんじが よめます。
examples.note: The object 漢字 takes が, the most natural particle with a potential verb.
来る has the irregular potential 来られる (こられる); the polite form is 来られます.

examples.reading: ここでは およげません。
examples.note: Potential + negative is the standard way to say what is not possible or not allowed.

examples.ja: この店では日本のお菓子が買えます。
examples.reading: このみせでは にほんの おかしが かえます。
examples.en: You can buy Japanese sweets at this shop.
examples.note: Potential form for possibility rather than personal skill: buying is possible here.

examples.ja: 昨日は疲れていて、何も食べられませんでした。
examples.reading: きのうは つかれていて、なにも たべられませんでした。
examples.en: I was tired yesterday and could not eat anything.
examples.note: 食べられる is the full Group 2 form; the JLPT does not accept 食べれる.

similarGrammar.difference: Same meaning, but longer and more formal. It is common in writing, announcements and rules (写真を撮ることができません).
For Group 2 verbs the passive and the potential look identical (食べられる). Look at the particles: potential usually has が on the object, passive has a person with に.
Potential + ようになる (話せるようになった) means you gained the ability over time. The plain potential just states that you can.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は日本語を分かれます。
commonMistakes.right: 私は日本語が分かります。
commonMistakes.why: 分かる already means "can understand", so it is never put into the potential form. The same is true of できる.

commonMistakes.wrong: 毎日、漢字を読めるように練習しています。→ 漢字を読めれます
commonMistakes.why: Group 1 potential is one step: 読む → 読める. Do not add another れる on top of a potential verb.

commonMistakes.wrong: 食べれる、見れる (in the exam)
commonMistakes.why: Dropping ら (ら抜き言葉) is very common in speech, but the JLPT treats the full られる form as correct.

usageNotes: Both 漢字が読める and 漢字を読める are heard; が is the textbook standard and the safer choice in the exam.
The potential form is used for possibility as well as ability: 駅から歩いて行けます (you can walk from the station).
見える and 聞こえる are separate verbs meaning "is visible / is audible" without effort; 見られる and 聞ける mean you are able to watch or listen (テレビが見られる = I can watch TV).
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断 the options often mix potential, passive and causative endings of the same verb (書ける / 書かれる / 書かせる). Check who is doing what: if the sentence is about ability, choose the え-row + る form.
Watch for 来られる (こられる) and できる: questions like 明日（　）ますか test whether you know the irregular potentials of 来る and する.
